- File: tests/test_dependency_registry_proxy.py
  Location: request() helper, lines 34-47
  Issue: A short client.recv after a silently-swallowed send failure is now only safe because the busy path happens to write its 503 before closing. If a future proxy change reorders send-then-close the other way, the test will hang on a 2-second recv instead of failing fast. There is no guard that the buffered reply actually arrived.
  Suggested minimal fix: After recv, assert the first three bytes are `b"503"` (or that the response starts with the expected status line) before returning, so a reordered close without a buffered reply surfaces immediately instead of returning empty bytes to the caller.
